bib.title: Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition

question: Is learning better networks as easy as stacking more layers, and how can the degradation of accuracy in very deep plain networks be fixed?
hypothesis: It is easier to optimize a residual mapping F(x)=H(x)-x than the original unreferenced mapping H(x); if identity were optimal, pushing the residual to zero is easier than fitting identity with nonlinear layers.
contributions: A residual learning framework with parameter-free identity shortcuts that eases training of much deeper networks
Evidence on ImageNet (up to 152 layers) and CIFAR-10 (up to 1202 layers) that plain nets degrade with depth while residual nets gain accuracy
ILSVRC 2015 1st place in classification (3.57% top-5 test ensemble), ImageNet detection, ImageNet localization, COCO detection and COCO segmentation

method.summary: Plain (VGG-inspired, 3x3 conv) and residual networks of matched depth, width and parameters are trained from scratch with SGD and BN on ImageNet and CIFAR-10. Residual blocks compute y=F(x,{Wi})+x with identity shortcuts (projection Ws only to match dimensions); 50/101/152-layer nets use a 1x1-3x3-1x1 bottleneck. Pretrained ResNet-50/101 are then fine-tuned in Faster R-CNN for detection and an RPN/R-CNN for localization.
method.task: image classification (ImageNet 2012, CIFAR-10), with transfer to object detection (PASCAL VOC, COCO, ImageNet DET) and localization

datasets.split: test on VOC07 test / VOC12 test

datasets.name: MS COCO
datasets.split: train 80k, eval on 40k val; later 80k+40k trainval for training, 20k test-dev for evaluation
datasets.preprocessing: shorter side s=600 pixels for single-scale

datasets.name: ImageNet DET

other.BN: statistics computed on ImageNet train set then fixed during detection fine-tuning

training.objective: classification softmax (implied by 1000-way fc with softmax); not named as cross-entropy
training.lr: ImageNet: 0.1; CIFAR-10: 0.1 (0.01 warm-up for 110-layer); COCO detection: 0.001 then 0.0001
training.lr_schedule: ImageNet: divided by 10 when the error plateaus. CIFAR-10: divided by 10 at 32k and 48k iterations, terminate at 64k. COCO detection: 0.001 for 240k iterations then 0.0001 for 80k iterations
training.warmup: CIFAR-10 110-layer only: lr 0.01 until training error below 80% (about 400 iterations), then back to 0.1
training.batch_size: ImageNet: 256; CIFAR-10: 128 on two GPUs; COCO: RPN 8 images, Fast R-CNN 16 images; localization fine-tuning 256
training.steps: ImageNet: up to 60 x 10^4 iterations; CIFAR-10: 64k iterations; COCO RPN and Fast R-CNN: 240k + 80k iterations
training.regularisation: batch normalization right after each convolution and before activation; no dropout; no maxout
training.seeds: ResNet-110 on CIFAR-10 run 5 times, reported best (mean+-std); other runs not stated

other.init: weights initialized as in He et al. 2015 [13]
other.framework: Caffe mentioned as an example of a common library
other.localization: 8 anchors sampled per image, positive:negative 1:1; R-CNN stage uses top 200 proposals per image, 224x224 warped crops
other.detection hyperparameters (VOC): same as Faster R-CNN [32]; not restated

inference.samples: ImageNet comparison studies: standard 10-crop testing; CIFAR-10: single view; ResNet-110 5 runs

other.best ImageNet results: fully-convolutional form, scores averaged over multiple scales with shorter side in {224, 256, 384, 480, 640}
other.final ensemble: six models of different depth, only two 152-layer ones at submission time
other.COCO multi-scale test: shorter side s in {200, 400, 600, 800, 1000}, two adjacent scales merged by maxout

limits: Authors concede the cause of the optimisation difficulty of deep plain nets is left for future study ('conjecture ... exponentially low convergence rates').
1202-layer net overfits on CIFAR-10 (19.4M params); stronger regularisation not tried.
Seeds and variance reported only for ResNet-110 on CIFAR-10; ImageNet results are single runs with no error bars.
No code, weights or compute/wall-clock figures stated in the paper; no parameter counts for ImageNet models.
Multi-scale training not done for COCO because of limited time; multi-scale testing only for the Fast R-CNN step.
Claim that residual learning is generic to non-vision problems is an expectation, not tested here.
Identity-mapping placement (ReLU after addition) was later revised by other work; not covered in this paper.

terms.definition: with the network depth increasing, accuracy gets saturated and then degrades rapidly; not caused by overfitting, adding layers leads to higher training error
F(x) := H(x)-x, with the original mapping recast as F(x)+x
shortcut connection that performs identity mapping, outputs added to the outputs of the stacked layers; adds neither extra parameter nor computation
three-layer residual function of 1x1, 3x3 and 1x1 convolutions where 1x1 layers reduce and restore dimensions
A: zero-padding for increased dimensions; B: projection for increased dimensions, others identity; C: all shortcuts projections
